clue.text: A sweetheart full of passion

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart, so flame means a lover

explanation.surface: A lover is described as consumed by ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ablaze with feeling is burning, glowing with ardour.

clue.text: Starts off if band can attempt dance music

indicators.note: starts off means each of the words if, band and can loses its opening letter

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A group strikes up a tune for dancing if they can try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' removes the opening letter of if, band and can, giving F, AND and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fandango is a lively Spanish dance, and the tune played for it.

clue.text: International everyone boycotts

parts.note: all means everyone
to black goods is to boycott them, as a trade union might

explanation.surface: A whole country is refusing to deal with a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: An All Black is a member of New Zealand's rugby union team, so an international player; to BLACK is a trade-union term for refusing to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Zealand national rugby player is capped at international level.

clue.text: Support for one behind sinecure in 7

explanation.surface: Support is offered to someone trailing for an easy job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is ACADEMIA: an undemanding professorship there is an easy chair. 'behind' is the buttocks, not following.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair supports the sitter's bottom, and an undemanding professorship is a cushy post.

clue.text: American planner spoils country house

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or damage it
a hall is a large manor house in the country

explanation.surface: An American designer ruins a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: George Marshall was the US Secretary of State behind the Marshall Plan for rebuilding post-war Europe. A HALL is a big English country house.
explanation.definitionFit: General George Marshall devised the Marshall Plan, so he is a famous American planner.

clue.text: Teacher soon becoming doctor's servant

parts.note: a mistress is a female schoolteacher
quickly means soon, without delay

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher rapidly turns into a physician's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor, Mistress Quickly is housekeeper to Doctor Caius.
explanation.definitionFit: This Shakespearean character keeps house for the French physician Caius, so she is his domestic.

clue.text: Get the bird in dispute, twice

parts.note: two words for a dispute: spar, to argue, and row, a quarrel
two words for a dispute: spar, to argue, and row, a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone is jeered at during an argument, two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' is theatre slang for being booed, a false trail; here the bird is just a small brown songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small common songbird.

clue.text: A rebel raised point in educational milieu

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the word for point goes in reverse

parts.note: to aim is to point

explanation.surface: A rebel lifts a point within a school setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIM to MIA in a down entry. Jack CADE is the leader of the 1450 Kentish rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: It's sounder to get to the front of the queue

parts.words: to get to the front of
parts.note: to lead is to be at the head
a line is a queue of people

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it is smarter to push to the head of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounder' is not 'more sensible': it means a thing that sounds, measuring water depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted cord dropped overboard measures the depth of water, a device for taking soundings.

clue.text: Study by dissecting a sort of snail, say

indicators.note: a sort of signals that the letters of the following words are made into a different kind of arrangement

explanation.surface: A biology lesson involves cutting up a kind of snail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' looks like it qualifies the snail, but it is the anagram signal applied to SNAIL and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis examines something by breaking it into its parts, just as dissection does.

clue.text: Something that goes to one's head in the country

definitions.text: Something that goes to one's head

explanation.surface: Something gets to someone's head while out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a straw hat worn on the head, and Panama is also a Central American nation.

clue.text: It's moving, elevating, and maintains suspense

definitions.text: It's moving, elevating, and maintains suspense

parts.words: It's moving, elevating, and maintains suspense
parts.note: reads like praise of a gripping, uplifting story, but describes a cabin that travels upward while hanging from a wire rope

explanation.surface: A thriller is praised as touching, uplifting and full of tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a car moves people uphill while hanging, literally suspended, from an overhead wire.

clue.text: One English novelist or another suffering cut

indicators.note: suffering a cut means the name loses its final letter here

parts.note: another English novelist: H. G. Wells

explanation.surface: One novelist or a rival is wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is a second English novelist, H. G. WELLS, who loses his last letter by 'suffering cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell, author of Animal Farm, was a British writer of novels.

clue.text: TV programme using singers in what way?

parts.note: chats are small songbirds, so singers stands for them
how means in what way

explanation.surface: A television show asks how it might feature vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singers' suggests vocalists, but CHATS are songbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: A talk show on television, where a host interviews guests, is a broadcast programme of this kind.

clue.text: Frightening place to be seated in plane?

definitions.text: place to be seated in plane?

explanation.surface: An air passenger finds the seat by the wing scary.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OVER A WING, the second part names a seat above an aircraft's wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Overawing means intimidating someone into submission, and a seat above the wing of an aircraft sits on one.

clue.text: A nation's music

explanation.surface: A country's songs are being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk can mean a people, a nation's population, and folk is also the traditional music of ordinary people.

clue.text: It's required when judging beauty

explanation.surface: Even-handedness is needed at a beauty contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartiality is essential for a judge, and fairness also once meant loveliness of face.

clue.text: It's child's play to advance by stages

explanation.surface: Making steady progress turns out to be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a playground game of vaulting over others, and to leapfrog is to move forward in bounds.

clue.text: Protect husband

explanation.surface: A wife is guarding her spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To save is to rescue or keep from harm, and to husband resources is to economise, keeping them back.

clue.text: Closing lines in theatre

parts.note: sounds like a play's final speeches, but means the threads a surgeon uses to close a wound in the operating theatre

explanation.surface: The final speeches of a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutures sewn to close a cut are drawn through as lines of thread in surgery.

clue.text: Poetry about a certain artist

indicators.note: about means the word for poetry goes round the next piece

parts.note: verse is poetry
one means a certain, as in one day

explanation.surface: Verse is written about a particular painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'a certain' stands for one as in 'one day'. Paolo Veronese was a sixteenth-century Venetian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a sixteenth-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: Roughly speaking, sport operated on a regular basis

indicators.note: roughly speaking says the words are said aloud and only approximately match the entry

parts.note: in biology a sport is a freak, an odd mutant plant or animal; operated means went, as a machine goes or runs

explanation.surface: A sports club ran its activities on a regular schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is not a game: in biology a sport is a FREAK, an odd mutation; operated is WENT (worked). Said together, roughly, FREAK WENT gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens often and habitually occurs regularly.

clue.text: Enthusiast may be, in fact, a loony

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters of the preceding words go wild

explanation.surface: A keen fan might actually be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loony' looks like a noun for the fan, but it is the anagram signal for IN FACT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot obsessed with a pursuit is an extreme devotee.

clue.text: Regret being put inside again?

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
pent means penned or shut in

explanation.surface: A prisoner regrets being jailed for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsy: someone shut up again is RE-PENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel remorse or sorrow for a wrong done.

clue.text: During first part of play, performing no business

parts.note: in means during, as in in the summer
Act I is the opening part of a stage play
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: An actor in the opening scene has nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is idleness, doing nothing at all, so there is no activity.

clue.text: Mistakes are holding Jack back

indicators.note: back means the whole combination is read from right to left
holding means the word are wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a jack, like a tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone excuses a sailor's errors by saying he is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole container, not just the sailor. A jack, like a tar, is crossword shorthand for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing errors listed in a book, so they are faults or slips.

clue.text: Given distinction, initially by the king, perhaps

definitions.text: Given distinction, initially by the king, perhaps

parts.words: Given distinction, initially by the king, perhaps
parts.note: describes someone honoured with a title, the sword-touch traditionally given by the monarch, and gaining the initial-free title Sir

explanation.surface: Someone is honoured, at first by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' tempts you to take the first letter of 'king', but the clue simply describes an honour conferred by a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dubbed a knight is an honour bestowed by the monarch, a mark of distinction.

clue.text: Result of deflation? A financial centre's prudence

parts.note: a tyre or balloon losing air will sag
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: An economist asks whether a banking capital's caution leads to falling prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deflation' reads as economics, but it is a balloon going down. THE CITY is London's banking quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is wisdom and good judgement, close to sound discretion.

clue.text: Mark, possibly, an essay gets most of the time

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a go

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the word for a period

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A student's essay mark takes up a great deal of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a grade, but it is the evangelist; 'essay' means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark's account of Christ's life is one of the four books of the New Testament so named.
